title: EchoBench: Consensus Is Not Corroboration — Measuring Epistemic Arbitration on a Synthetic Social Web
description: Benchmark for epistemic arbitration in web-enabled language models. 100 claims × 6 counterfactual conditions (600 worlds, 14 pages/world) with hidden provenance graphs. Hybrid BM25+MiniLM search, deterministic metrics (FBAR/CUR/EAS/PCR/ICS/SER/PSR/PRR/CI/TUA/calibration/cost), clustered bootstrap CIs, sealed test split (480 worlds). This release covers 14 frontier model configurations run on the dev split, 13 of which clear the completeness/rejection-rate eligibility rule, compared on 16 shared episodes. One eligibility rule drives every table and figure, every displayed value maps to a run set in paper/run_manifest.json, and paper/build_paper.py regenerates all tables and figures from the manifest and score reports. See paper/main.pdf and PREREG.md.
